result.title: HistGramBench: Measuring Structural Recovery When Multimodal Models Redraw Historical Mathematical Diagrams as TikZ
result.summary: Digital libraries preserve mathematical books printed from the sixteenth to the twentieth century, but the lettered diagrams in them, the figures on which Euclidean proofs depend, remain scanned images whose content cannot be searched. Redrawing such a diagram as a short drawing program would record which points lie on which lines and circles. But a printed plate offers no source code against which the redrawing could be checked. We introduce HistGramBench, a benchmark of 2,507 diagrams from 95 works printed between 1551 and 1933 in eight languages. For each diagram, two AI models from different providers agree on the facts a reader takes from the figure, such as which lines are parallel or where two lines meet, and every redrawing is checked against those facts on the model's own drawing. We evaluate six affordable AI models. The best recovers about three fifths of these facts, and most of what the models miss comes from programs that never produce a drawing. Parallels and tangencies are the hardest relations to reproduce. HistGramBench gives historians and librarians a way to measure when such tools can make old mathematical diagrams searchable.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 HistGramBench，包含 1551–1933 年间八种语言数学书籍的 2507 幅插图；用两个不同厂商模型对「哪些线平行、哪些线相交」等结构事实达成共识作为检验标准，评测六个低成本多模态模型把图重绘为 TikZ 程序时能恢复多少这些事实，最优模型约恢复五分之三。
AI.relevance_reason: 该基准直接诊断多模态模型能否从图保留几何与实体关系等任务必要信息，其「程序未产出绘图即整体失败」以及平行、相切关系最难恢复的结论，可供核查视觉证据筛选与结构保真问题；但只涉及一次性图像到代码生成，不涉及 latent 推理状态、动态计算或停止决策。
